metadata.note: Passenger rail at Oswego, NY - a Lake Ontario port that was a hub for three railroads (the New York Central, the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western, and the New York, Ontario & Western) and has had no passenger service since 1951. This layer covers the Syracuse-Oswego corridor: the Oswego and Syracuse Railroad of 1848, under DL&W management from 1872, which ran through Baldwinsville, Lamsons, South Granby, Fulton and Minetto - the traced route passes within 1.8 km of all seven of the line's own stations. It connects to the New York Central main line already on the map at Syracuse. NOT INCLUDED: the New York, Ontario & Western, whose main line ran 400-odd miles from Oswego (its namesake northern terminus, promoted by DeWitt C. Littlejohn of Oswego) to Weehawken NJ and which in 1957 became the first Class I railroad abandoned in its entirety - its corridor survives at Oswego as the 'O&W Pedestrian Promenade and Bikeway' but tracing the whole abandoned main line was out of scope here; and the RW&O/NYC 'Hojack' line west along the Lake Ontario shore toward Niagara Falls. Geometry is real OSM corridor; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates. The Binghamton-Syracuse half of this same DL&W Syracuse Branch is a separate layer, syracuse_and_binghamton_railroad.geojson.
sources: http://nyrails.org/railroads/delaware-lackawanna-and-western-railroad/dlw-syracuse-branch/ -- New York Railroad Archive (DL&W Syracuse Branch passenger operations ended Syracuse-Oswego in February 1949 and Syracuse-Binghamton in September 1958; the branch ran about 114 miles Binghamton to Oswego with 30 stations)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswego_and_Syracuse_Railroad (formed Apr 29 1839, organized Mar 25 1847, opened May 14 1848, 35.5 miles Syracuse to Oswego; consolidated with the Syracuse, Binghamton and New York in 1853; leased by the DL&W Feb 13 1869 and under its management from 1872)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: SOURCE CONFLICT RESOLVED 2026-08-24: this feature previously ended in 1951, citing Wikipedia attributing the last trains on the corridor to the New York Central. Two independent sources now date the end of DL&W Syracuse-Oswego passenger service to February 1949, one giving Feb 13 1949, so the segment has been cut back to 1949 -- under Rule 1, drawn years must not assert passenger service that cannot be evidenced. The 1951 claim is not necessarily wrong about the New York Central: the NYC reached Oswego over its own trackage, and if NYC trains ran there until 1951 they did not run on this alignment. That has not been checked, and no source has been found for a last NYC Oswego train. Headways in all three segments remain estimates, and the 1949 date is a discontinuation date rather than a documented last train.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The Oswego and Syracuse Railroad was formed April 29, 1839, fully organized March 25, 1847 and opened May 14, 1848, running 35.5 miles from Syracuse to Oswego with stations at Syracuse, Baldwinsville, Lamsons, South Granby, Fulton, Minetto and Oswego, per Wikipedia. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: The line passed under Delaware, Lackawanna and Western management in 1872. Into the mid-1940s the DL&W ran daily passenger service from Hoboken through Binghamton and Syracuse, ending at Oswego. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Postwar decline. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western discontinued passenger service between Syracuse and Oswego on Feb 13 1949. Oswego has had no passenger rail since. This feature previously ran to 1951 on the strength of a Wikipedia statement attributing the final trains to the New York Central; see not_yet_sourced. Headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_source: Geometry traced from the surviving corridor (CSX's Baldwinsville Subdivision, largely disused) using the OpenStreetMap API - Overpass was unavailable, so the rail network was walked way-by-way from Oswego via node/<id>/ways lookups and routed with a shortest-path search (ODbL). Douglas-Peucker simplified to ~50 m.
